knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The WorkSafe Victoria licence page gives the WP class for boom-type elevating work platforms (reviewed 30 June 2026) [R5]. The same page says scissor lifts do not need a WP licence, and a stepladder or water-fed pole is not a platform.
The Queensland licence rule excludes platforms shorter than 11 metres (QLD-11, confirmed). The other options are not part of that exclusion.

Before a platform is raised, a written rescue plan must exist and the operator's licence must be checked where a licence is required. A customer signature, a discount or a ladder does not meet this need.
A licence covers the licensed operator and the platform type. It does not cover other crew members or the business as a whole, so the crew cannot rely on one licence.
An elevated platform rate needs evidence of licence, equipment and authority. General worker experience alone does not support it.

practicalCriteria: The learner identifies the platform type and states the state rule that applies, or names the check to make.
The learner checks the operator's licence class and validity and records them before the platform moves.
The learner writes a rescue plan naming who carries it out, before the platform is raised.
The learner sets a drop zone with barriers or a supervisor and records it.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80% correct (4 of 5). Practical sign-off is assessed separately. A knowledge pass does not verify operator competence or licence status.
evidenceRequired: Platform type and state rule record
Operator licence details with class, validity and issuing regulator
Written rescue plan and platform inspection record
Drop zone record and quote with exclusions
stopWorkCriteria: The operator has no current licence where one is required for the platform type.
The platform is raised without a written rescue plan.
The drop zone cannot be kept clear of people and property.
The learner relies on a licence held by a different worker.
